question.text: Explain why you need a common denominator before you add 1/3 + 1/6. Use an example.
question.modelAnswer: Fractions can only be added directly when the parts are the same size. Thirds are bigger than sixths, so change 1/3 into 2/6. Then 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6, which is 1/2.

question.text: Why does ice float on water? Explain using the idea of density.
question.modelAnswer: When water freezes its molecules form an open structure, so ice takes up more space for the same mass. Its density is lower than liquid water, and objects less dense than water float.

criteria.description: Ice is less dense than liquid water and less dense things float

levels.description: Says ice is less dense or lighter for its size, without linking to floating

levels.description: Lower density than water, and less dense objects float

levels.label: Partial

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Same mass in a larger volume because molecules form an open structure

responses.answer: Ice is less dense than liquid water, and anything less dense than water floats. It is less dense because when water freezes the molecules lock into an open pattern, so the same mass takes up more volume.
Ice floats because it is less dense than water. Water expands when it freezes.
Ice floats because it is cold and cold things are lighter.
Ice has air bubbles in it so it floats.
Ice is lighter for its size than water. That's it.
When water freezes the molecules spread out into a crystal, so the ice has the same mass but bigger volume, which means lower density. Lower density than water means it floats.
Density is mass divided by volume. Ice takes up more space than the water it came from.
Ice floats because it is solid and solids float on liquids.
